decisions.decision: Committee agreed to let the superintendent and business manager revisit their capital request after an earlier presentation, given the newness of the process.
Committee plans to meet both the following two Wednesdays (Dec 10 and Dec 17), aiming to hold Dec 10 in person.
The track and field complex will be treated as a capital item run in parallel with the regular capital plan, likely needing a separate town meeting article.

If an FY27 IT request is confirmed, the committee will not rank priorities next week and will wait an extra week; if not confirmed, members will bring their prioritized rankings to next week's meeting instead.
No move to shift police cruisers from the capital plan to the operating budget this year, since the useful-life threshold has not changed.
Next meeting set for 7 p.m., an earlier time than usual because of a school committee meeting conflict.
Minutes from October 29 and November 5 were tabled for review at the next meeting.

minutes.headline: School district resubmitted a revamped multi-year capital plan; committee will rank FY27 priorities over the next two meetings
minutes.summary: The Capital Planning Committee heard a redone FY27-30 capital presentation from the superintendent and business manager after an earlier, less complete version, covering completed FY25 projects and new requests spanning Turkey Hill and primary school facilities, safety systems, a generator, an auditorium upgrade, and IT and vehicle items. No capital items were voted on; the committee agreed to schedule two more meetings to finalize and rank a prioritized list, and tabled approval of prior minutes.

what_happened.line: The district resubmitted a reworked FY27-30 capital plan after an earlier version was deemed incomplete, and no items were voted on.
The committee scheduled two more meetings, aiming to hold December 10 in person, to finalize and rank FY27 capital priorities.
New FY27 requests span security cameras and window film, a generator, an auditorium audio/access upgrade, a heated maintenance garage, and vehicle and IT items.
The track and field complex will be handled as a separate capital item running alongside the regular plan, likely needing its own town meeting article.
A late-arriving FY27 IT network request may push the ranking timeline back a week if it is confirmed.

why_it_matters: This ranking process will shape what capital spending -- school security systems, a generator, playground and driveway work -- goes forward for a FY27 town meeting vote.
The track and field complex being treated as a separate capital item signals it may appear as its own warrant article and borrowing question, distinct from the regular capital plan.
Safety-related items like door intercoms/cameras and window film are framed as replacing systems past their useful life, which residents may hear about again as specific budget lines.
watch_next: Committee meetings on Wednesday, December 10 (in person) and December 17, to rank and finalize the FY27 capital priority list
Confirmation of the FY27 IT network request, which determines whether ranking happens next week or is delayed
